scope: Union of structured observations from attempts 003 and 004; not a retrospective ledger or teacher input
deduplication: Manual grouping by same trigger and mechanism, preserving complete per-attempt records and run-scoped evidence IDs
count_note: Structured arrays contain 12 observations grouped into eight mechanisms. The review mentions nine; a ninth observation in prose is possible but not identified here. No ninth structured finding was invented.

finding.description: A positive max_chunk_size below one page can leave a fresh job permanently unable to prefill.
finding.trigger: Use max_chunk_size=128 with an uncached 600-token prompt and initial kv_position=0.
finding.expected_behavior: Reject an unusable chunk size or ingest a positive number of prompt tokens.
finding.actual_behavior: The endpoint rounds down to zero; prefill continues without inference or progress, and the job remains ineligible for decoding on subsequent iterations.

verification.description: Evaluated the inspected endpoint formula for a 600-token prompt. Chunk sizes 128 and 255 produced endpoint zero; 256 produced 256 and 2048 produced 599.
verification.limits: Integer arithmetic only; no Job or model implementation executed.

observations.review_disposition: retained observation; individual confirmation not inferred

finding.description: Sub-page chunk sizes can stall prompt ingestion.
finding.trigger: max_chunk_size is between 1 and 255, a sequence has uncached prompt tokens to ingest, and its KV position starts at zero.
finding.expected_behavior: Either validate a page-sized minimum or ingest a positive number of prompt tokens.
finding.actual_behavior: Prefill rounds the endpoint down to zero and continues because prefill_end <= prefill_start. The sequence remains unready and subsequent iterations repeat without progress.

verification.description: For a 300-token prompt at position zero, chunk 255 produced endpoint zero; chunks 256 and 2048 produced endpoints 256 and 299 respectively.
verification.limits: Endpoint arithmetic only; no prefill model call.

finding.description: Enqueue-time capacity validation omits private pages for all but the last sequence.
finding.trigger: Enqueue a two-sequence job with 100 prompt tokens and max_new_tokens=100 per sequence into a one-page cache, with max_batch_size at least two.
finding.expected_behavior: Reject the impossible two-page request during preparation.
finding.actual_behavior: prepare_for_queue() accumulates all_unique_pages but calculates total_pages using only the last seq.new_unique_pages. It accepts the one-page estimate; current_new_pages_required() later correctly requests two pages, preventing admission indefinitely.

verification.description: Modeled the two inspected capacity formulas: enqueue estimate one page, scheduler requirement two pages, cache capacity one page.
verification.limits: No actual enqueue or scheduler loop was executed.

observations.review_disposition: retained observation; individual confirmation not inferred

finding.description: Enqueue validation omits private pages from all but the last sequence.
finding.trigger: A multi-sequence job's total private-page requirement exceeds cache capacity, while its shared context hashes plus the last sequence's private pages fit. For example, two one-token sequences requesting 100 output tokens each with a one-page cache.
finding.expected_behavior: Reject the impossible request during preparation using the union of context hashes plus every sequence's private-page count.
finding.actual_behavior: prepare_for_queue accumulates all_unique_pages but calculates total_pages using only seq.new_unique_pages from the last loop iteration. Admission later sums every sequence correctly, so the example is enqueued with a reported requirement of one page but permanently needs two; repeated iteration cannot start it.

verification.description: Computed the inspected page formulas for the two-sequence example: private pages [1,1], enqueue total 1, admission requirement 2, capacity 1.
verification.limits: Exact small-integer arithmetic, not execution of the scheduler.

finding.description: Cancelling an AsyncJob does not wake a consumer already waiting on its empty result queue.
finding.trigger: A consumer is suspended at await self.queue.get() when another coroutine calls AsyncJob.cancel().
finding.expected_behavior: The cancelled job's asynchronous iterator terminates without needing another result.
finding.actual_behavior: Cancellation removes the job from the generator and sets cancelled=True, but supplies no queue sentinel or waiter cancellation. The flag is checked only before the pending queue.get(), so that consumer can remain suspended.

verification.description: Ran a minimal asyncio model of the flag check and empty-queue wait. After setting the cancellation flag and yielding to the loop, the consumer task was still pending.
verification.limits: This modeled the wait mechanism, not the repository wrapper or inference.

observations.review_disposition: retained observation; individual confirmation not inferred

finding.description: Cancelling a job does not wake an already waiting async iterator.
finding.trigger: An AsyncJob consumer is suspended on queue.get with an empty queue when another coroutine calls AsyncJob.cancel.
finding.expected_behavior: The waiting consumer should terminate or receive a cancellation signal.
finding.actual_behavior: Cancellation removes the underlying job and sets cancelled=True, but provides no queue sentinel and does not cancel the waiting consumer. The flag is checked only before queue.get, leaving the existing wait suspended.

verification.description: Ran a minimal asyncio consumer with the inspected flag-check/queue-get ordering. After setting the cancellation flag and yielding, consumer_done_without_queue_signal remained false; the harness then explicitly cancelled it.
verification.limits: Exercises asyncio queue behavior in a transcription, not AsyncJob or inference.

finding.description: Enabling draft decoding reduces the terminal output-token threshold by the configured draft length.
finding.trigger: Generate without healing or other stop conditions using max_new_tokens=100 and num_draft_tokens=4.
finding.expected_behavior: Draft lookahead should not itself terminate the response before the requested 100-token budget.
finding.actual_behavior: receive_sample() terminates when new_tokens reaches 96 because it compares against max_new_tokens−num_draft_tokens. With both values equal to four, the first generated token already satisfies the cutoff.

verification.description: Computed the first positive counter satisfying the source predicate: 100 for budget/draft 100/0, 96 for 100/4 and one for 4/4.
verification.limits: Only the stopping predicate was evaluated; no draft acceptance or model execution was tested.

observations.review_disposition: retained observation; individual confirmation not inferred

finding.description: Banned-string rewind restores a differently named attribute instead of the token buffer used for emission.
finding.trigger: A banned-string match reaches rewind_checkpoint() before the max-token termination branch.
finding.expected_behavior: Restore held_tokens to the checkpoint alongside held_text and the other held buffers, keeping rejected tokens out of ordinary token_ids output.
finding.actual_behavior: The code assigns self.held_token, singular. emit() still reads self.held_tokens, plural, which retains the rejected suffix and can emit it as token_ids despite rewinding the sequence and text.

verification.description: Compared the checkpoint assignment with the held_tokens buffer initialized by prepare_for_queue() and consumed by emit().
verification.limits: No banned-string generation or native string matcher was executed.

observations.review_disposition: retained observation; individual confirmation not inferred

finding.description: Banned-string rewind restores the wrong token-buffer attribute.
finding.trigger: A full banned-string match reaches rewind_checkpoint before a terminal branch, including a one-token match such as 'bad' with a larger output budget.
finding.expected_behavior: Restore held_tokens to the checkpoint and report rejected IDs only as suppressed_tokens, keeping emitted tokens consistent with rewound sequence state.
finding.actual_behavior: rewind_checkpoint assigns checkpoint['held_tokens'] to self.held_token. The actual self.held_tokens buffer retains rejected IDs; emit_held subsequently emits and clears that stale buffer while also reporting the IDs as suppressed.

verification.description: Modeled the inspected attribute assignments with a rejected ID 7 and an empty saved buffer. The sequence rewound, but both emitted_token_ids and suppressed_tokens remained [7].
verification.limits: List/attribute model; SeqTensor copying and KV invalidation were inspected, not executed.

finding.description: Requested chosen-token probabilities and top-token outputs do not reach their prepared streaming buffers.
finding.trigger: A job reaches receive_logits with return_probs=True or return_top_tokens greater than zero.
finding.expected_behavior: Return the requested final sampling probabilities and top-token arrays alongside the sampled token, allowing receive_sample to buffer and emit them.
finding.actual_behavior: The enabled branches execute only pass. return_probs=True leaves next_prob unassigned; return_top_tokens>0 leaves next_k_tokens and next_k_probs unassigned. The return tuple therefore raises UnboundLocalError. CustomSampler.forward supplies only token IDs and receives no request for these additional outputs.

verification.description: Traced flags through sampling, tuple unpacking, held buffers and emitted field names.
Executed the same conditional assignments with a scalar token: disabled flags returned four values; each enabled option raised the corresponding unbound-local error.
verification.limits: Checks Python control flow, not distribution computation or tensor shapes.

finding.description: Draft decoding sizes its batch by jobs while populating it by sequences.
finding.trigger: Draft decoding is enabled and a ready job contains multiple sequences.
finding.expected_behavior: Allocate and index one draft row per sequence, or reject multi-sequence drafting explicitly.
finding.actual_behavior: iterate_draftmodel_gen increments batch_size once per ready job, then increments batch for every sequence when writing block_index and cache_seqlens. One two-sequence job allocates one row but attempts to populate two, before collective sampling can occur.

verification.description: Compared the job-count sizing loop with the nested sequence-writing loop and ordinary iterate_gen's sequence-count sizing.
verification.limits: The exact first PyTorch exception was not measured.

finding.description: The output-budget branch can emit a banned string without checking it.
finding.trigger: A non-stop token completes a banned string exactly when the token-budget condition becomes true; for example, a single token decoding to 'bad', banned_strings=['bad'], max_new_tokens=1 and no draft model.
finding.expected_behavior: Apply banned-string suppression before flushing terminal held output.
finding.actual_behavior: receive_sample returns through the max_new_tokens branch with emit_held=True before reaching banned-string matching, emitting the banned text and token IDs.

verification.description: Checked the inspected terminal predicate for the one-token example: 1 >= 1-0 is true, selecting the flush branch before matching.
verification.limits: Branch-order model assumes the stated token decoding; no tokenizer or native matcher execution.

completeness: Non-exhaustive. Empty findings means none noticed, not defect-free.
